main.t: One of two bones forming the upper jaw, most of the hard palate and part of the orbit floor (maxilla).

simpler.t: The maxilla is your upper jaw bone.

deeper.t: It contains the largest paranasal sinus, the maxillary sinus, just below the orbit.

facts.t: The two maxillae meet in the midline to form the upper jaw.
Each forms the inner (medial) floor of the orbit and the side of the base of the nose.
Its lower edge holds the upper teeth.

simpler.t: It forms your upper jaw, just below the eye.

deeper.t: With the palatine bones, it forms the hard palate between the mouth and the nose.

items.name: Alveolar process
items.t: The curved lower edge that holds the upper teeth.

items.name: Infraorbital foramen
items.t: An opening just below the orbit, for a sensory nerve to the nose, upper lip and front of the cheek.

items.name: Palatine process
items.t: A shelf that meets its partner to form the front three-quarters of the hard palate.

items.name: Orbital surface
items.t: Forms most of the inner floor of the orbit.

items.name: Maxillary sinus
items.t: The largest paranasal sinus, below the orbit.

simpler.t: It has a ridge holding the upper teeth, a shelf forming the roof of the mouth and a large sinus.

deeper.t: Each tooth sits in a deep socket called an alveolus.

facts.t: Its alveolar process anchors the upper teeth in deep sockets.
Its palatine processes meet in the midline, separating the mouth from the nasal cavity.
The large maxillary sinus lightens the skull, but its opening is high on the inner wall, so it drains poorly.

simpler.t: It holds your upper teeth and forms most of the roof of your mouth.

items.name: Upper teeth
items.t: Each tooth root is held in its socket by a fibrous joint (gomphosis).

items.name: Palatine bones
items.t: Their horizontal plates complete the back quarter of the hard palate.

items.name: Sensory nerve to the face
items.t: Leaves through the infraorbital foramen to supply the nose, upper lip and front of the cheek.

items.name: Orbit
items.t: The maxilla forms most of its inner floor, with a small part from the palatine bone.

items.name: Nasal cavity
items.t: The hard palate forms its floor, and the maxilla the side of the base of the nose.

simpler.t: It holds the upper teeth and joins the palatine bones, the orbit and the nose.

facts.t: The right and left maxillae come together in the midline during embryonic development.
Like the other flat bones of the face, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
facts.check: OpenStax 6.4 says the flat bones of the face form from membrane, but 7.5 says the facial bones form from cartilage; which applies to the maxilla needs an approved source.

facts.t: In childhood the jaws grow as the teeth appear, and the sinuses enlarge.

items.injury: A sinus infection, often after a cold.
items.damaged: The maxillary sinus, the sinus most often infected.
items.cannotDo: Clear the sinus easily: pressure and pain build below the eye.
items.why: The sinus opens into the nasal cavity high on its inner wall, so it drains poorly.

items.injury: A blow to the eye from in front, as from a ball.
items.damaged: The thin floor of the orbit breaks into the maxillary sinus below (blow-out fracture).
items.why: An eye muscle and orbital fat can be trapped in the break.

items.q: Explain why the maxillary sinus is the one most often infected.
model: It is the largest paranasal sinus.
Its connection to the nasal cavity is high on its inner wall.
So it is difficult to drain.
Trapped fluid and mucus allow infection and cause pressure and pain.

items.q: Compare the parts the maxillae and the palatine bones play in the hard palate.
model: The palatine processes of the maxillae form the front three-quarters.
The horizontal plates of the palatine bones form the back quarter.
All four meet in the midline.
Together they separate the mouth from the nasal cavity.

items.q: A sensory nerve leaves the skull through the infraorbital foramen. Predict where a patient is numb if it is injured.
model: On the same side as the injured nerve.

check.stem: Which is the largest paranasal sinus?
check.why: The maxillary sinus is the largest.

check.stem: Which part of the hard palate do the maxillae form?
check.why: Their palatine processes form the anterior three-quarters of the hard palate.

check.stem: What does the alveolar process of the maxilla hold?
check.why: It contains the sockets of the upper teeth.
